In theory, a CEO is just a person who is in charge of running a company on behalf of its owners. General consensus is that all CEOs are bad due to the actions of a few. I've had a few arguments/discussions about this in the past so I thought I would take the time to point out 2 different things here.

I'm going to skip the actual terms, such as CIO and CFO and proper titles like non managing directors and so on. Also the question in the title is rhetorical, but feel free to ask questions.

Its a story about a company that grows.

A man starts a business. There is an OWNER. He is the sole member of the business. He is the CEO and all the STAFF members. He does the accounting, sales, purchasing, distribution and labour for service or production.

* OWNER

The man makes enough to live and has more customers than he can service. He hires a young person for some manual labour. That young person takes on some of the responsibilities above, but the core business decisions are still done by the OWNER as he is also the CEO.

* OWNER * 1 STAFF

Time goes on and the business grows. The OWNER is no longer able to run the business from his home. He hires a part time staff member to do administration work, freeing up more time for the OWNER and the existing STAFF member. They also hire a small office.

* OWNER * 2 STAFF

The OWNER and the original STAFF member realise that they can copy and paste their business into another suburb that seems to have a market for their business. They hire 2 more people to do what the OWNER and the original STAFF member have been doing for another location. The part time admin staff is now full time.

* OWNER * 4 STAFF

The OWNER has good control over the business operations and the STAFF he has hired. They are quality people and demand for business rises beyond capacity. To reduce all the time that the OWNER spends doing labour work, he hires a new STAFF member to replace him. The business expands to 2 more locations, 4 more STAFF and they start to rent out more buildings. An extra ADMIN staff member is hired full time.

* OWNER * 10 STAFF

Business is booming. The locations it service are now at capacity. One new STAFF member is hired for each location. Business is growing well and they can save long term costs on buying their own office/warehouse/store buildings. They stop renting and now own 4 buildings.

* OWNER * 14 STAFF

The OWNER has set up a sustainable business. It now runs itself. Each site has one supervisor, 2 workers and half an admin STAFF member dedicated to make sure all their paperwork is done. The OWNER now has experience and understands his business and market. He now wishes to focus on expanding the business and no longer wants to spend the time managing it. He hires a general business manager.

* OWNER * GM * 14 STAFF

The business units the OWNER has created seems to have been sustainable for each area. The GM is able to maintain business levels. The OWNER opens up 4 more businesses across the country. Each one starting with 2 staff (the goal to increase by 1 more once the business takes root in those locations) and half an admin worker.

* OWNER * GM * 24 STAFF

The OWNER realises that there is a new product/service that is similar to his current business, but different enough that he can not just lump it together with the existing one. He decides to remove himself from the business. He has set up procedures and expectations and knows that his GM can continue to run and expand the show as he wanted to. He makes the GM the CEO. He promotes the original young worker to the new GM and hires a new staff member to replace him. The OWNER is no longer the CEO, but he is able to withdraw the funds from the business and is able to push the CEO when he wants to, because he is now the BOARD OF DIRECTORS (This can be expanded on, but I will not in this example) and the OWNER.

* OWNER * CEO * GM * 24 STAFF

The Owner goes away from the business and starts a new one, BUT, he has ultimate control of the business, because it is STILL his business, but the CEO makes all the decisions on his behalf.

While the OWNER is away the CEO quadruples the business over the next 5-10 years. He hires CFOs, CIOs, various managers and buys a large office building to host them and their admin staff.

* OWNER * CEO * VARIOUS LEVELS OF MANAGERS AND OTHER OFFICES * 100+ STAFF

Now, the two points I mentioned.

1. The CEO is not the person you should hate when you hate a company.

2. A CEO is a profession that you can not hate just because that is their title.
